On this page

Getting Started ​

Saidi is a hosted workspace. There is nothing to install and nothing to run — you create an account, name a workspace, and brief your first department.

Free while in early access

Every feature is open during early access: unlimited departments, agents, runs, schedules and reflexes, and no seat cap. Usage is metered in credits, and while early access lasts the credits are on us.

1. Create your account ​

Open the app and choose how you want to sign in:

MethodWhat happens
Email + passwordYou receive a verification link. Your account is limited until you click it.
GoogleOne redirect, no password to manage.
GitHubSame, and the identity you will most likely want when connecting repos.

Which providers appear on the login screen depends on what the platform has configured; email and password are always available.

2. Name your workspace ​

A workspace (an org, internally) is the boundary around everything you create: agents, runs, chats, memory, schedules, reflexes, connections and the credit ledger. Nothing crosses between workspaces.

The first person to create a workspace is its owner. You can belong to more than one and switch between them from the account menu.

Joining instead of creating

If a colleague invited you, open their invite link rather than creating a workspace. The invite is locked to the email address it was sent to, and it carries the permissions the sender chose for you.

3. Set your guardrails — before anything runs ​

Do this now, not after your first surprise. In Settings:

SettingWhereWhy it matters first
Approval modeApprovalsDecides whether consequential actions pause for a human or proceed.
Spend ceilingCosts & LimitsA hard cap, checked before a call is made.
Tool permissionsApprovalsPer-agent control over what may read, write, run or publish.

Agents write to real systems

Saidi commits and pushes to branches on repositories you connect, and can send mail and call external services. It never merges and never force-pushes — but set the approval mode and the ceiling you are comfortable with before your first autonomous run. See Approval & Spend Guardrails.

4. Meet the console ​

The left rail is the whole product:

SectionWhat lives there
HomeYour departments and agents at a glance — click one to look inside.
ChatWhere you brief Saidi. Multiple conversations, each with its own thread.
RunsEvery durable unit of work: in flight, waiting on you, or finished.
SchedulesRecurring runs on a cron.
ReflexesEvent triggers — a push lands, a run fails, a webhook fires.
MemoryWhat the workspace has learned and carries between runs.
MarketSkills, connectors, agents and whole departments to install.
SettingsProviders, costs, approvals, connections, team.

Chat is where you talk to PRIME — the orchestrator you brief. Everything else is a window onto what PRIME did.

5. Invite your team ​

From Settings → Team, send an invite and pick that person's permissions as you do it. Runs and chats belong to whoever created them: no role, not even owner, reads another member's work unless it is explicitly shared with them.
